script.base: SF is a 1.5-point home favorite with both teams implied in the low 20s (SF 23.0, ARI 21.5), so this stays competitive into the fourth quarter and neither backfield is a garbage-time committee. Arizona has been balanced-to-run-lean through two games (48 rushes vs 52 targets): James Conner is the closer at 23 carries for 73 yards (games 39 and 34), Kyler Murray has already taken 13 carries for 72 yards, and Trey Benson is the change-up at 11 carries. When San Francisco blitzes — they have blitzed 30% — Arizona's EPA/db falls from 0.19 to 0.08, so the base pass script is short, with Trey McBride (16 targets, 139 yards) as the safety valve and Marvin Harrison Jr. (11 targets, 103 air yards) not required to win the game. San Francisco's side of the script is Christian McCaffrey all afternoon (35 carries, 17 targets) because a 1.5-point spread does not bench him. Pace is moderate on a 44.5 total.
script.flip1: Brock Purdy is questionable with a shoulder and the pack does not name a replacement (M.Jones has 3 rushes for 9 yards and is not confirmed as the starter). If Purdy sits or is capped, San Francisco's downfield game — Ricky Pearsall 235 air yards, Jauan Jennings 133 air yards and himself questionable with an ankle — stalls, McCaffrey checkdowns become the offense, and a Cardinals lead turns into Conner and Murray clock work. That flip helps both Arizona unders below; it would kill any 49ers receiver over. Inactives are not in the pack, so the base case is Purdy plays until the 90-minute report says otherwise.
script.flip2: Arizona's offensive line is the other live flip: Will Hernandez (knee) and Paris Johnson Jr. (knee) are both questionable. If they are limited or out, pressure rises on top of the 30% blitz, rushing efficiency falls, and Arizona abandons the run. Conner and Benson rush yards die, McBride's short targets rise, and Harrison's air yards do not convert. The variance flip inside that script is one explosive: San Francisco has allowed 3 runs of 10+ and 5 passes of 20+ on 60 attempts, and Benson already has a 69-yard rushing game, so a single chunk play can cash an under without changing the score.

Arizona has been sound outside (left 5.17 on 35, right 4.18 on 34) and relatively soft in the middle (7.3 YPA on 30 attempts). matchup.pressure: This is the usable scheme edge. San Francisco blitzes 30 percent. Arizona's EPA per dropback is 0.08 against the blitz and 0.19 when not blitzed, so pressure already taxes this offense and should cut deep receiving yards while pushing checkdowns to McBride and the backs. Arizona blitzes only 14 percent. San Francisco's EPA per dropback is 0.62 when blitzed and 0.11 when not, so the 49ers are comfortable if Arizona brings extra rushers — and Arizona mostly does not. Burford being out adds a separate 49ers protection issue that is not an Arizona-blitz story.
matchup.bleeds: San Francisco rush defense allows 3.66 yards per carry with 3 runs of 10+ in two games — a real front, not a bleed. Their pass defense, weighted by the attempt counts in the pack, is about 6.4 YPA, dragged down by the right side and not rescued by a 7-attempt middle. Arizona rush defense allows 3.92 YPC with 4 runs of 10+. Arizona's pass defense is the tighter unit in the pack, about 5.5 YPA weighted, with the middle (7.3 on 30) the only area that actually bleeds. Explosive passes: SF defense 5/60, ARI defense 5/103.
matchup.overlap: Arizona's primary target is McBride (16 targets, 31 percent of the 52 team targets, 139 yards). He is the player who would attack the short and middle area the blitz opens. That overlap would be a receptions edge, and receptions are not an available market. His receiving-yard line is 69.5 against games of 61 and 78, so the stand-in already prices his full role, and the same blitz that adds targets also drops Arizona EPA. He does not clearly beat 69.5. The overlap that is mispriced in an allowed market is the inverse: Benson's 41.5 rush line assumes 7.55 YPC from an 11-carry back against a 3.66 YPC front, and Harrison's 49.5 assumes his 9.4-air-yard profile survives a 30 percent blitz that has already cut Arizona's EPA in half.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and the Benson under lost because one run did it. San Francisco has allowed 3 runs of 10-plus in two games, and Benson's own 69-yard game is the template: RB2 volume plus one explosive clears 41.5 without Conner sitting. The two-game carry total of 11 also might hide a role change if the 69 came with Conner limited and the 14 was the real script, and we do not have per-game carry splits to kill that story. Hernandez and Paris Johnson both playing and Arizona leading would add carries, but even 10 carries at this defense's 3.66 rate is about 37, so volume is not the counter-case — the long run is. That counter is why the leg is flagged and not sized. It is not stronger than the share math, so the strong read stays. The Harrison under loses if he aligns to the left side that allows 8.56 YPA on 27 attempts and connects on another 71-yard day, or if Arizona falls behind and the 11-target, 103-air-yard profile finally cashes against a defense that has allowed 5 passes of 20-plus. That counter is close, which is why Harrison is a lean and not a strong, and why he is not a building-block leg. McBride over was the overlap candidate and lost the pre-mortem: 69.5 is his mean, and the blitz that would feed him also drops Arizona EPA from 0.19 to 0.08.
slip_story: One script, two Arizona unders, no parlay required. The story is a close outdoor game, SF 23.0 and ARI 21.5, in which Conner and Murray keep the valuable carries, San Francisco's 3.66 YPC front does not pay 7.5 YPC to the RB2, and a 30 percent blitz plus questionable Arizona tackles tax Harrison's air yards while McBride is the unbettable short answer. Both legs win together if Arizona does not hit chunk plays. Both lose together if the explosives show up. Do not add a game total over, a Pearsall or Harrison over, a McCaffrey receiving over, or Benson rush-plus-rec — those need the flip this slip is fading. No touchdowns, no receptions market, no second market on either player, no stake. Purdy questionable is a flip that helps this slip if he sits, and it is not a reason to add 49ers overs.
